name: Larmor collapse of the classical atom
summary: By the Larmor formula, a classical electron orbiting a proton radiates and spirals in within about 10^-11 s. This instability of Rutherford's atom forced Bohr's quantization, and it is resolved by the stationary states of the quantum hydrogen atom.

name: Mie partial waves, optical theorem, Born approximation
summary: Mie theory expands the scattered field in vector spherical harmonics with coefficients a_n, b_n, exactly as quantum partial-wave analysis uses phase shifts δ_l. The optical theorem began as optical extinction, and Rayleigh–Gans scattering is the first Born approximation.
breaks: Light is a vector field: there are two multipole families (TE and TM) and no monopole term, so the Mie sum starts at n=1.
sources: Mie (1908). "Beiträge zur Optik trüber Medien, speziell kolloidaler Metallösungen". *Ann. Phys.* 330, 377. [doi:10.1002/andp.19083300302](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19083300302)
Born (1926). "Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge". *Z. Phys.* 37, 863. [doi:10.1007/BF01397477](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01397477)

name: Hellings–Downs curve as a spatial coherence function
summary: A stochastic GW background is a Gaussian random field that, like partially coherent light, can only be detected by cross-correlating separated receivers; the Hellings–Downs curve is the angular correlation of pulsar timing residuals for an isotropic spin-2 background, the analogue of the mutual coherence function versus baseline.
map: \Gamma(\zeta)=\tfrac32x\ln x-\tfrac{x}{4}+\tfrac12,\ x=\tfrac{1-\cos\zeta}{2}\ \leftrightarrow\ \Gamma_{12}(\mathbf b)\propto\int I(\hat s)e^{-ik\mathbf b\cdot\hat s}d\Omega
breaks: The correlated quantity is a redshift integrated along the line of sight with a quadrupolar spin-2 response, not a field amplitude at a point; pulsar terms add uncorrelated noise, and a background from a finite source population has cosmic variance.

name: Aperture synthesis images black-hole shadows
summary: Each VLBI baseline samples one spatial-frequency component of the sky brightness (van Cittert–Zernike), so the Earth-sized EHT is a sparse Fourier-plane aperture whose image is recovered by regularized inversion at λ/D ≈ 20 μas; the ~42 μas ring of M87* tests the predicted Kerr shadow size.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ab0ec7](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ab0ec7)

Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. IV. Imaging the Central Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L4. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ab0e85](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ab0e85)

name: Eikonal limit: null geodesics, photon sphere, shadow
summary: The short-wavelength limit of Maxwell's equations on a curved background gives rays along null geodesics, with a parallel-transported wave vector and conserved photon number; the photon sphere at 3GM/c² and the critical impact parameter √27 GM/c² that sets the shadow are geometric-optics results, computed by backward ray tracing.

name: Weak-field lensing as an effective refractive index
summary: In a weak static field light moves as if in a medium of index n = 1 − 2Φ/c², so Fermat's principle gives the deflection 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value, and the Shapiro delay is the excess optical path; the lens equation is ray optics with an achromatic thin lens.
breaks: Valid only for weak, static fields; the index is achromatic and comes half from time curvature and half from space curvature (PPN γ); strong fields need full null geodesics.

name: Wave-optics (diffractive) lensing of gravitational waves
summary: When a GW's wavelength is comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of a lens, geometric optics fails and the Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction integral gives a frequency-dependent amplification factor that imprints interference and diffraction on the waveform; this is a target for searches in LIGO and LISA data.
map: F(w,\mathbf y)=\frac{w}{2\pi i}\int d^2x\,e^{iwT(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)},\quad w=\frac{4GM_{Lz}\,\omega}{c^3}

name: Michelson interferometry reads out spacetime strain
summary: LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA are Michelson interferometers held near a dark fringe; a passing wave changes the differential arm length by ΔL = hL, which appears as an output phase shift amplified by Fabry–Pérot arm cavities and recycling to reach strain noise ~10^-23/√Hz.
sources: Abbott et al. (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Time-delay interferometry for unequal-arm LISA
summary: LISA's 2.5 million km arms cannot be held equal, so laser frequency noise would swamp the signal; LISA records one-way heterodyne phases between spacecraft and recombines them in post-processing with time shifts (TDI) to synthesize equal-arm Michelson and Sagnac interferometers.

name: Michelson–Morley null ether-drift interferometer
summary: The 1887 interferometer looked for a fringe shift ∝ (v/c)²L/λ on rotation, caused by Earth's motion through the ether, and saw less than about a twentieth of the expected 0.4 fringe; the result was a key empirical input to special relativity and the template for every later two-arm isotropy test.
sources: Michelson & Morley (1887). "On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether". *Am. J. Sci.* 34, 333. [doi:10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333](https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333)
Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: EHT polarimetry maps horizon-scale magnetic fields
summary: Stokes-parameter imaging of the synchrotron emission from M87* and Sgr A* shows ordered spiral linear polarization; the pattern and its Faraday rotation through the magnetized accretion flow constrain the field geometry and favour magnetically arrested disks.

name: Plus/cross: spin-2 analogue of linear polarization
summary: GWs have two transverse polarizations (+, ×) that, like light's two linear states, combine into circular helicity states and admit Stokes-like parameters for stochastic backgrounds; but + and × differ by a 45° rotation, not 90°, because a rotation by ψ multiplies helicity-h amplitudes by e^{ihψ}.
map: h_+\pm ih_\times\to e^{\pm2i\psi}(h_+\pm ih_\times)\ \leftrightarrow\ E_x\pm iE_y\to e^{\pm i\psi}(E_x\pm iE_y)
breaks: A tensor wave produces a quadrupolar tidal strain on a ring of test masses rather than a force on a charge, and there is essentially no gravitational medium, so GR has no counterpart of crystal birefringence.

name: Vacuum birefringence as a Lorentz-violation probe
summary: Lorentz-violating photon terms (SME k_F, Carroll–Field–Jackiw) make the vacuum birefringent, so polarization rotates or splits in proportion to distance and frequency; polarimetry of gamma-ray bursts, AGN and the CMB constrains these coefficients to the 10^-32 level and below.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Maxwell's equations force special relativity
summary: Maxwell's equations are invariant under Lorentz, not Galilean, transformations; the moving-magnet/conductor asymmetry and null ether-drift experiments led Lorentz, Poincaré and Einstein ('On the electrodynamics of moving bodies', 1905) to rebuild kinematics around an invariant c, which then fixed the form of every later field theory.
map: c=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}\ \text{in every inertial frame}\Rightarrow x'^\mu=\Lambda^\mu{}_\nu x^\nu
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)
Michelson & Morley (1887). "On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether". *Am. J. Sci.* 34, 333. [doi:10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333](https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333)

name: Gertsenshtein effect: graviton–photon conversion
summary: A GW crossing a static magnetic field sources an EM wave of the same frequency through the field's stress–energy coupling (Gertsenshtein 1962), and vice versa; this mixing underlies proposals to detect MHz–GHz gravitational waves with strong magnets and microwave cavities like those of axion haloscopes.

name: Interstellar plasma dispersion in pulsar timing
summary: Radio pulses crossing ionized interstellar plasma travel at a group velocity set by the plasma frequency (the same dispersion relation as a waveguide above cutoff) and arrive late by an amount ∝ DM/f²; PTAs observe at several frequencies to fit and remove this chromatic delay, a dominant noise in nanohertz GW searches.

name: Dynamical Casimir effect and moving-mirror radiation
summary: Time-dependent boundary conditions on a cavity or transmission line mix positive and negative frequencies and create photon pairs from vacuum; this is the moving-mirror model (Fulling–Davies) that reproduces Hawking's thermal flux, and it was observed in 2011 with a SQUID-modulated superconducting transmission line.

name: Rotating resonant cavities as modern Michelson–Morley
summary: Modern isotropy tests compare the resonance frequencies of orthogonal cryogenic optical or microwave cavities on rotating platforms; any direction dependence of c shifts their beat note, which bounds photon-sector Standard-Model-Extension coefficients near the 10^-17–10^-18 level.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)
Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Blandford–Znajek: spinning hole as unipolar inductor
summary: A Kerr black hole threaded by magnetic flux behaves like Faraday's spinning-disk dynamo: frame dragging drives an EMF across field lines, currents close through the force-free magnetosphere and the horizon's resistance, and rotational energy leaves as Poynting flux; this is the leading model for jets from magnetically arrested disks.
sources: Blandford & Znajek (1977). "Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 179, 433. [doi:10.1093/mnras/179.3.433](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/179.3.433)

name: Gravitoelectromagnetism and frame dragging
summary: For weak fields and slow sources the metric perturbations h_00 and h_0i act as gravito-electric and gravito-magnetic potentials obeying Maxwell-like equations sourced by mass density and mass current; frame dragging (Lense–Thirring, measured by Gravity Probe B and LAGEOS) is the gravitomagnetic field of a spinning mass.
map: h_{00}\leftrightarrow\phi,\ h_{0i}\leftrightarrow A_i,\ \rho\leftrightarrow\rho_q,\ \rho\mathbf v\leftrightarrow\mathbf J,\ \epsilon_0\to-1/(4\pi G)
breaks: Holds only at linear order and for slow motion; factors of 2 and 4 depend on convention because the source is a spin-2 tensor; like masses attract, there are no negative masses or gravitational dipole radiation, and full GR is nonlinear.

name: Gauge connections: vector potential vs Christoffel
summary: The vector potential is a U(1) connection whose curvature is F and whose holonomy is the Aharonov–Bohm phase; in GR the Christoffel (or spin) connection plays the same role, Riemann is its curvature, and parallel transport around a loop measures it, so both are theories of connections on bundles.
breaks: Gravity gauges spacetime itself (diffeomorphisms) and adds a metric/tetrad with no Maxwell counterpart; the Einstein–Hilbert action is linear in curvature while Maxwell's is quadratic, and there is no fixed background.

name: Proca photon vs massive graviton (Stückelberg, vDVZ)
summary: A photon mass breaks gauge invariance, but the massless limit is smooth because the Stückelberg scalar decouples; the same Stückelberg trick applied to Fierz–Pauli massive gravity exposes a helicity-0 mode that does not decouple (vDVZ discontinuity), cured nonlinearly by Vainshtein screening and dRGT; both masses are bounded by wave dispersion (m_γ ≲ 10^-18 eV, m_g ≲ 10^-23 eV).
breaks: The spin-1 massless limit is continuous and the spin-2 one is not: the graviton's scalar mode couples to T and changes linear-order light bending to 3/4 of the GR value; massive gravity also has the Boulware–Deser ghost, which Proca lacks.

name: Lorenz gauge ↔ harmonic gauge in linearized gravity
summary: Linearized GR is a gauge theory of h_{μν} with δh_{μν} = ∂_μξ_ν + ∂_νξ_μ; in Lorenz (de Donder) gauge the trace-reversed perturbation obeys a sourced wave equation solved by retarded potentials exactly like A^μ, and the residual gauge freedom gives TT gauge with two transverse polarizations, as Coulomb/radiation gauge does for light.
breaks: The field is rank 2 (helicity ±2 vs ±1); the gauge group is linearized diffeomorphisms, which beyond linear order become non-abelian and act on spacetime itself; source conservation ∂T = 0 is consistent only at linear order.

name: Ashtekar variables: GR as an SU(2) gauge theory
summary: Ashtekar recast GR's phase space as an SU(2) connection A^i_a conjugate to a densitized triad E^a_i that acts as a non-abelian 'electric field'; loop quantum gravity then quantizes Wilson-loop holonomies and electric fluxes, so area becomes discrete like quantized flux lines.
breaks: Gravity adds the Hamiltonian and diffeomorphism constraints, which have no Yang–Mills counterpart, and the Barbero–Immirzi parameter γ; discrete area is a prediction of the quantization, not of the gauge-theory form.

name: Einstein–Maxwell theory: charged black holes
summary: The traceless Maxwell stress–energy tensor sources Einstein's equations; solving the coupled Einstein–Maxwell system gives the Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman black holes, with inner and outer horizons and an extremal limit Q = M in geometrized units.

name: Kaluza–Klein: Maxwell from five-dimensional gravity
summary: Compactifying 5D general relativity on a circle turns the off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} into a U(1) gauge field obeying Maxwell's equations, with charge as momentum around the circle and gauge transformations as reparametrizations of the extra coordinate; it is the template for gauge fields from geometry in string compactifications.
map: ds_5^2=g_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu+\phi^2(dy+\kappa A_\mu dx^\mu)^2;\ y\to y-\kappa\lambda\Leftrightarrow A_\mu\to A_\mu+\partial_\mu\lambda
breaks: An extra radion scalar φ appears and must be stabilized; charge quantization ties e to the circle radius, and the minimal theory cannot produce chiral fermions, which string theory gets from richer compactifications.

name: Covariant Lorentz force as relativistic dynamics
summary: The covariant Lorentz force dp^μ/dτ = qF^{μν}u_ν is the prototype relativistic equation of motion: the antisymmetry of F keeps u·u fixed, so rest mass is conserved, and it gives the relativistic cyclotron frequency qB/(γm) that forced the move from cyclotrons to synchrotrons.

name: E and B as components of one Lorentz tensor
summary: Under a boost E and B mix as components of the antisymmetric tensor F^{μν} = ∂^μA^ν − ∂^νA^μ, so magnetism is electrostatics seen from a moving frame; E² − c²B² and E·B are the Lorentz invariants that classify fields.
map: F'^{\mu\nu}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta F^{\alpha\beta};\ \mathbf E'_\perp=\gamma(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)_\perp,\ \mathbf E'_\parallel=\mathbf E_\parallel
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: Membrane paradigm: horizon as a 377 Ω conductor
summary: For external static observers the stretched horizon behaves as a 2D conducting membrane whose surface charges and currents terminate field lines, with surface resistivity equal to the impedance of free space; a charge lowered toward a hole has its field lines drawn onto the horizon like the induced charge on a conducting sphere.
breaks: The membrane is a fictitious bookkeeping surface with no charge carriers, and it is teleological: it responds to fields before they arrive. The description fails for observers falling through the horizon.

name: Fresnel drag as relativistic velocity addition
summary: Fizeau (1851) found that light in flowing water is dragged by the fraction 1 − 1/n² of the flow speed, which Fresnel put down to partial ether drag; von Laue (1907) showed it is exactly the first-order relativistic addition of c/n and v.

name: Kerr multipole moments and the no-hair theorem
summary: A stationary spacetime has Geroch–Hansen mass and current multipole moments analogous to those of a static charge distribution; for Kerr all of them are fixed by M and a, so an independent measurement of the quadrupole −Ma² (EMRIs with LISA, ringdown spectroscopy, pulsar–black-hole timing) tests the no-hair theorem.

name: Multipole radiation: Larmor to the quadrupole formula
summary: Gravitational radiation is organized by the same multipole expansion as EM radiation, but conservation of mass and momentum removes the monopole and dipole terms, so the leading emission comes from the reduced mass quadrupole with power ∝ (d³Q/dt³)², paralleling Larmor's ∝ (d²p/dt²)².
map: P_{GW}=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle\ \leftrightarrow\ P_{EM}=\frac{\mu_0\ddot p^2}{6\pi c}
breaks: Gravity is spin-2 and has one sign of charge, so there is no dipole radiation; it is nonlinear, the radiated energy itself gravitates (Isaacson tensor, memory), and the expansion uses tensor rather than vector harmonics.

name: Superradiance: Kerr black hole as an amplifier
summary: Waves with ω < mΩ_H that scatter off a Kerr hole are amplified by tapping its rotation (Zel'dovich–Starobinsky superradiance, the wave form of the Penrose process); Bekenstein read this as stimulated emission paired with spontaneous Hawking emission, and a mirror or a massive field's own potential turns the gain into a laser-like 'black-hole bomb' instability.
breaks: The gain comes from horizon rotation, not population inversion, and it saturates as the hole spins down; ultralight-boson clouds (current research) radiate continuous GWs rather than light.

name: Stabilized lasers and Fabry–Pérot cavities in GW detectors
summary: Interferometric GW detection rests on laser engineering: 1064 nm Nd:YAG-based lasers frequency-stabilized by Pound–Drever–Hall locking, mode-cleaner cavities, km-scale Fabry–Pérot arms, and power/signal recycling that builds up hundreds of kW of circulating light, which sets the shot-noise floor.

name: Transformation optics: spacetime geometry as a medium
summary: Maxwell's equations on a curved spacetime, or in transformed coordinates, are the same as those in flat space with an impedance-matched anisotropic medium ε = μ (Plebanski; Gordon's optical metric for moving media); transformation optics inverts the map to design cloaks and metamaterial analogues of black holes, Einstein rings and cosmic strings.
breaks: Only light propagation on a fixed geometry is mimicked, with no gravitating dynamics; dispersion and loss restrict it to narrow bands, and g_{0i} ≠ 0 requires magnetoelectric coupling.
sources: Leonhardt (2006). "Optical Conformal Mapping". *Science* 312, 1777. [doi:10.1126/science.1126493](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1126493)

name: Fibre-optical event horizons and analogue Hawking light
summary: A soliton in a fibre raises the refractive index through the Kerr effect; in its co-moving frame, probe light slower than the pulse cannot cross the front, which forms black/white-hole horizon pairs, and the frequency conversion observed there is the stimulated analogue of Hawking emission.
breaks: Strong optical dispersion regularizes the trans-Planckian region, so the spectrum is not exactly thermal; there is no gravity, entropy or backreaction, and claims of spontaneous analogue Hawking photons in bulk glass are disputed.

name: Squeezed light from OPOs beats detector shot noise
summary: Optical parametric oscillators (χ(2) down-conversion below threshold) generate squeezed vacuum that is injected at the dark port, cutting shot noise by about 2–3 dB in LIGO and Virgo since O3; in O4 a 300 m filter cavity rotates the squeezing angle with frequency so that radiation-pressure noise is not raised at low frequency.
sources: Walls (1983). "Squeezed states of light". *Nature* 306, 141. [doi:10.1038/306141a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/306141a0)

name: Parametric down-conversion ≡ particle creation
summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion and Hawking, Unruh or cosmological particle creation are the same Bogoliubov transformation of mode operators: the output is a two-mode squeezed vacuum that looks thermal when one partner mode is traced out, with the temperature set by the squeeze parameter.
map: \hat b_1=\cosh r\,\hat a_1+\sinh r\,\hat a_2^\dagger,\ \langle n\rangle=\sinh^2r;\ \text{Hawking: }\tanh r=e^{-\pi\omega/\kappa}\ (\hbar=c=1)
breaks: In optics the pump is an external classical field acting through a χ(2) medium; in gravity the 'pump' is the spacetime geometry, and the partner modes lie behind a horizon.

name: Vacuum Cherenkov radiation bounds Lorentz violation
summary: Cherenkov emission needs v > c/n; if Lorentz violation made the vacuum photon phase speed lower than a particle's maximal speed, charged particles above a threshold would radiate in vacuum, so the survival of TeV–PeV electrons and protons from cosmic-ray and gamma-ray sources bounds Standard-Model-Extension coefficients.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Dipole radiation as a signature of scalar–tensor gravity
summary: GR forbids gravitational dipole radiation, but in scalar–tensor theories bodies with different scalar charges (sensitivities) emit scalar dipole radiation at −1PN relative to the quadrupole, just as an EM dipole radiates when charge-to-mass ratios differ; binary-pulsar and GW inspiral timing bound it tightly.

name: Radiation reaction: Abraham–Lorentz vs 2.5PN
summary: Radiation back-reacts on its source: through the Abraham–Lorentz(–Dirac) force for charges and the Burke–Thorne 2.5PN potential for masses, whose integration gives the Peters–Mathews inspiral and chirp; the gravitational self-force programme (MiSaTaQuWa) mirrors the DeWitt–Brehme treatment of point charges.
breaks: EM reaction is dipolar (third time derivative) and gravitational reaction is quadrupolar (fifth derivative, 2.5PN); the gravitational self-force is gauge dependent, and the runaway solutions of ALD have no clean gravitational analogue.

name: Accelerated-charge radiation and the Unruh bath
summary: Seen from the co-accelerating frame, the Larmor radiation of a uniformly accelerated charge is emission and absorption of zero-energy Rindler photons from the thermal Unruh bath (Higuchi–Matsas–Sudarsky 1992); this ties a classical radiation formula to the Unruh effect and to the equivalence-principle puzzle of whether a supported charge radiates.

name: Black-hole scattering: partial waves, glory, orbiting
summary: Wave scattering by a black hole is solved with the partial-wave and Regge-pole methods of Mie theory; the cross section shows a backward glory and orbiting oscillations tied to the photon sphere, and in the eikonal limit its Regge poles are the quasinormal modes.
breaks: A black hole is a perfect absorber with a long-range 1/r potential (Coulomb-like phase, divergent forward cross section), unlike a finite dielectric sphere.

name: HBT intensity interferometry → Bose–Einstein femtoscopy
summary: Hanbury Brown and Twiss measured star sizes from intensity correlations. Goldhaber, Goldhaber, Lee and Pais (1960) found the same Bose–Einstein enhancement for like-sign pions, and LHC experiments now use it to measure femtometre source radii in pp, p–Pb and Pb–Pb collisions.

name: Beam optics: ray-transfer matrices for magnet lattices
summary: Transverse beam dynamics uses ABCD ray-transfer matrices: drifts are free propagation, quadrupoles are thin lenses, and a FODO cell of alternating converging and diverging lenses gives net focusing (strong focusing). Chromaticity is the beam-optics version of chromatic aberration and is corrected with sextupoles.
breaks: A quadrupole focuses in one transverse plane and defocuses in the other, so net focusing needs alternating gradients. Beams also have emittance (Liouville in 6D phase space), space charge and nonlinear resonances, which passive optics lacks.

name: Diffractive elastic pp scattering as Fraunhofer diffraction
summary: High-energy elastic pp scattering (TOTEM at 13 TeV) shows a forward peak and a diffraction dip, like the Airy pattern of an absorbing disc in the momentum transfer √(−t). The optical theorem ties the forward amplitude to σ_tot, and a black disc would have σ_el/σ_tot = 1/2.
breaks: The proton is grey (σ_el/σ_tot ≈ 0.26 at 13 TeV) and grows with energy (Froissart ln²s). Its amplitude has a real part and spin dependence, so a single disc cannot fit the dip depth.

name: Axion-induced vacuum birefringence and dichroism
summary: With the coupling g a E·B, only the photon polarization component parallel to an external B mixes with an axion-like particle. A magnetized vacuum therefore becomes dichroic (real conversion) and birefringent (virtual axions), which PVLAS-type polarimeters search for. An oscillating axion background rotates linear polarization; this is the proposed explanation for a ~2–3σ hint of CMB cosmic birefringence.
map: -\tfrac{g_{a\gamma\gamma}}{4}aF_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{\mu\nu}=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\ \Rightarrow\ \text{only }\mathbf E_\gamma\parallel\mathbf B_{\rm ext}\text{ mixes}

name: Flavour oscillation as birefringence; MSW as adiabatic following
summary: Two neutrino flavours behave like two linear polarizations, and the mass eigenstates like the axes of a birefringent plate, so the conversion probability has the same form as light leaking through crossed polarizers. Solar MSW conversion is the analogue of light adiabatically following the axes of a slowly twisted birefringent medium (the Poincaré/Bloch-sphere picture).
breaks: There are three flavours with a CP-violating phase and an absolute mass ordering, while light has only two polarization states. The phase comes from mass differences, not refractive-index differences.

name: Maxwell theory as abelian Yang–Mills
summary: Covariant electrodynamics is the U(1) case of Yang–Mills theory: the same action, field strength and field equations. Yang–Mills adds a commutator term that makes gluons and W bosons self-interacting, while photons do not interact with each other.
breaks: The non-abelian commutator gives cubic and quartic self-couplings, asymptotic freedom and confinement, none of which classical electromagnetism has.

name: Haloscope: axions drive a resonant microwave cavity
summary: In a static field B₀, dark-matter axions act as an oscillating effective current g ȧ B₀. This current drives the TM₀₁₀ mode of a tuned cavity when ω = m_a c²/ħ, as in Sikivie's haloscope (ADMX, HAYSTAC). Sensitivity depends on standard cavity quantities: mode form factor, volume, Q and tuning range.

name: Waveguide cutoff modes = Kaluza–Klein mass tower
summary: Confining a massless field in compact transverse directions quantizes its transverse momentum. Each guided mode then follows a massive-particle dispersion relation along the free direction, with the cutoff frequency playing the role of the Kaluza–Klein mass.
breaks: Conducting walls impose Dirichlet/Neumann conditions instead of periodicity, so TE/TM spectra (and the missing TM zero mode) differ from a KK circle, and the waveguide geometry produces no gauge field.

name: RF cavities accelerate collider beams
summary: Beams gain energy from the longitudinal E field of the TM₀₁₀ mode of resonant cavities. The achievable gradient (~30–40 MV/m for superconducting niobium in the ILC, ~70–100 MV/m for normal-conducting X-band in CLIC) sets the length and cost of linear colliders.

name: Axion electrodynamics: modified Maxwell equations
summary: Adding g a E·B to the Maxwell Lagrangian gives effective charge and current densities proportional to ∇a and ȧ. These are the field equations behind haloscopes, helioscopes and stellar-cooling bounds. The same equations with constant θ = π describe the magnetoelectric response of topological insulators.

name: Kaluza–Klein: electromagnetism from a fifth dimension
summary: Five-dimensional general relativity on a small circle reduces to 4D gravity plus Maxwell theory plus a scalar. The off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} play the role of A_μ, and U(1) gauge transformations are reparametrizations of the circle. This is the ancestor of modern large and warped extra-dimension models.

name: Magnetic monopoles: Dirac quantization and GUT monopoles
summary: A magnetic charge makes Maxwell's equations symmetric, and Dirac showed that a single monopole would force electric charge to be quantized. Breaking a simple GUT group down to U(1)_em necessarily creates 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of mass ~M_X/α. Their predicted overabundance helped motivate inflation; MoEDAL and IceCube searches have found none.
map: \nabla\cdot\mathbf B=\rho_m,\quad qg=2\pi n\ (\hbar=c=1,\ \text{HL}),\quad M_{\rm mon}\sim M_X/\alpha_{\rm GUT}

name: Quantized Maxwell field: the first quantum field theory
summary: A normal-mode expansion turns the free Maxwell field into independent harmonic oscillators, and quantizing them (Dirac 1927) gives photons. Gauge redundancy forced the Coulomb-gauge, Gupta–Bleuler and later BRST treatments that became the template for quantizing every gauge field.
map: H=\sum_{\mathbf k,\lambda=\pm}\hbar\omega_k\left(a^\dagger_{\mathbf k\lambda}a_{\mathbf k\lambda}+\tfrac12\right),\quad [a_{\mathbf k\lambda},a^\dagger_{\mathbf k'\lambda'}]=\delta_{\mathbf k\mathbf k'}\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}

name: Gauge transformations and the covariant derivative
summary: The freedom A→A+∂χ of electromagnetic potentials, paired with a local phase change of charged matter fields, is the gauge principle. Yang and Mills extended it to non-abelian groups, where A becomes a matrix-valued connection and the potentials become the fundamental fields.

name: Aharonov–Bohm phase as the Wilson loop
summary: The Aharonov–Bohm phase around a solenoid is the holonomy of the U(1) connection. Wilson made these parallel transporters the basic lattice variables (link variables) and used the Wilson loop as the order parameter for confinement (area law).
map: U_{x,\mu}=e^{iagA_\mu(x)},\quad W(C)=\prod_{\ell\in C}U_\ell\to e^{\frac{iq}{\hbar}\oint_C\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf l}=e^{iq\Phi_B/\hbar}

name: Thomas–BMT spin precession and the magic momentum
summary: The muon g−2 experiment measures how much faster the spin precesses (Thomas–BMT equation) than the momentum rotates, in a 1.45 T storage ring with field mapped by proton NMR. At γ = 29.3 (3.094 GeV/c) the motional-E term from electrostatic focusing cancels, so a_μ follows from ω_a and B alone. Fermilab's final result (2025) reached 127 ppb.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Weizsäcker–Williams photons in ultraperipheral collisions
summary: Lorentz contraction flattens an ultrarelativistic charge's field into a transverse pancake, equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons with a spectrum ∝ Z²α/ω. With the Z⁴ enhancement, Pb–Pb ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC act as a photon–photon collider, where light-by-light scattering and γγ→ℓℓ are measured.

name: E·B invariant as the chiral-anomaly density
summary: The pseudoscalar Lorentz invariant FF̃ ∝ E·B is the U(1) Chern–Pontryagin density. As a total derivative it has no classical effect, but it sources the ABJ anomaly: π⁰→γγ, and chiral charge pumping when E and B are parallel (the chiral magnetic effect).
sources: Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

name: The photon as the unbroken U(1)_em combination
summary: Maxwell theory is the massless U(1) that survives when the Higgs breaks SU(2)_L×U(1)_Y. The electron charge is fixed by g, g′ and the weak mixing angle, and the Z is the orthogonal, massive combination — classical electrodynamics is the low-energy remnant of electroweak theory.

name: Shockley–Ramo theorem: signals from weighting fields
summary: The current that a drifting charge induces on a readout electrode (silicon strips and pixels, wire chambers, TPC pads) follows from Green's reciprocity. One solves Laplace's equation with that electrode at unit potential and all others grounded, and the induced current is the charge's velocity dotted into this weighting field.
map: i(t)=q\,\mathbf v(t)\cdot\mathbf E_w(\mathbf x(t)),\quad \nabla^2\phi_w=0,\ \phi_w|_{\rm readout}=1,\ \phi_w|_{\rm others}=0

name: Coulomb's law as the photon propagator
summary: The Green's function of Poisson's equation is the Fourier transform of the static one-photon-exchange propagator 1/q². In the Born approximation, tree-level exchange of a massless boson gives the 1/r potential and a massive one gives Yukawa's e^{-mr}/r.

name: Vacuum polarization: the vacuum as a dielectric
summary: Virtual e⁺e⁻ pairs screen a bare charge the way bound charges do in a dielectric, so the effective charge grows at short distances (the Uehling potential). The running α(Q²) behaves like a scale-dependent permittivity, rising from 1/137 to about 1/128 at m_Z.
breaks: Lorentz invariance forces εμ = 1 for the vacuum (there is no rest frame), the response depends on q² rather than on frequency alone, and the screening is UV-divergent. The bare charge cannot be observed, so it has to be renormalized.

name: Asymptotic freedom as vacuum paramagnetism
summary: Since εμ = 1 for a relativistic vacuum, antiscreening (ε < 1) is the same thing as paramagnetism (μ > 1). In the Nielsen–Hughes picture, the Pauli paramagnetism of spin-1 gluons outweighs their orbital Landau diamagnetism and quark screening, which gives the sign of the QCD β-function.
breaks: The picture is one-loop and perturbative. It says nothing directly about confinement, and the constant chromomagnetic background it uses is unstable (Nielsen–Olesen).

name: Magnetic spectrometry: momentum from track curvature
summary: Collider detectors measure momentum from how much charged tracks bend in solenoid or toroid fields (the 3.8 T CMS solenoid, the ATLAS toroids), designed from Biot–Savart field maps. Because the sagitta shrinks as 1/p, momentum resolution degrades in proportion to p.

name: MAC-E filter: adiabatic magnetic collimation (KATRIN)
summary: Tritium β electrons spiral along a field that falls by ~10⁴ from the source to the analysing plane. Adiabatic invariance of the magnetic moment converts transverse into longitudinal energy, so an electrostatic retarding potential becomes a sharp high-pass filter. KATRIN used this to set m_ν < 0.45 eV (90% CL, 2025).

name: 2D multipole expansion of accelerator magnets
summary: Accelerator magnet fields are written as a complex 2D multipole series: dipoles bend, quadrupoles focus, sextupoles correct chromaticity and octupoles damp instabilities. LHC magnet quality is specified by the error coefficients b_n and a_n, in units of 10⁻⁴ at R_ref = 17 mm.

name: Electric dipole moments as P- and T-odd multipoles
summary: A permanent EDM along a particle's spin is odd under both P and T, so by CPT it signals CP violation. Electron (ACME, JILA) and neutron EDM limits probe CP violation far beyond the tiny CKM-phase prediction and constrain baryogenesis models.
map: H=-\mu\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf B-d\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E,\quad P,T:\ \boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E\to-\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E

name: E1/M1 radiative transitions in quarkonium
summary: Radiative decays such as ψ(2S)→γχ_cJ (E1) and J/ψ→γη_c (M1) obey the same multipole selection rules and rate formulas as atomic transitions. They were used to map the charmonium and bottomonium spectra and to test potential models.

name: Plasma frequency as photon mass: Anderson's route to Higgs
summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω² = ω_p² + c²k², the dispersion relation of a massive photon. From plasmons and the Meissner effect, Anderson (1963) argued that gauge bosons can gain mass without a leftover Goldstone boson. Englert–Brout, Higgs and Guralnik–Hagen–Kibble made this precise, and it became electroweak symmetry breaking.
breaks: A plasma picks out a rest frame and breaks Lorentz invariance, and its longitudinal plasmon is not the W's longitudinal mode. The Higgs vacuum is Lorentz-invariant and has a physical scalar left over.

name: Euler–Heisenberg: the QED vacuum as a Kerr medium
summary: Integrating out the electron leaves four-photon operators suppressed by 1/m_e⁴, which act as a third-order susceptibility χ⁽³⁾ of the vacuum. This predicts light-by-light scattering, observed by ATLAS and CMS in ultraperipheral Pb–Pb collisions, and vacuum birefringence in strong fields, which has not yet been seen in the laboratory.

name: Strong-field QED at the laser intensity frontier
summary: Chirped-pulse amplification pushes laser fields toward the Schwinger critical field. Once the normalized amplitude a₀ ≫ 1, multiphoton processes stop being perturbative in the laser field, so nonlinear Compton scattering and multiphoton Breit–Wheeler pair creation (SLAC E144) are computed with laser-dressed Volkov propagators (Furry picture).

name: Cherenkov and transition-radiation particle ID
summary: RICH and DIRC detectors measure β from the Cherenkov angle, which together with the tracker momentum gives the mass and separates π, K and p (LHCb, ALICE, Belle II). Transition-radiation detectors such as the ATLAS TRT separate electrons from pions using the γ-dependence of transition-radiation yield.

name: Cherenkov light as the neutrino detector
summary: Water and ice detectors (Super-K, SNO, IceCube) see neutrino interactions through the Cherenkov cones of the charged secondaries. A sharp ring marks a muon and a fuzzy ring an electron shower, and the cone direction points back to the source. At EeV energies, coherent Askaryan radio emission from the shower's charge excess takes over (ARA, RNO-G).

name: Synchrotron loss sets collider size and choice of particle
summary: The relativistic Larmor (Liénard) power of a charge on a circular orbit grows as γ⁴/R², so the energy lost per turn limits circular e⁺e⁻ machines (the size of FCC-ee and CEPC). This pushes designs toward linear colliders or muons, which radiate (m_e/m_μ)⁴ ≈ 5×10⁻¹⁰ times less.

name: Angular ordering from coherent soft radiation
summary: In the QED Chudakov effect, a fresh e⁺e⁻ pair radiates soft photons mainly inside its opening angle, because outside it the pair looks neutral and the two amplitudes cancel. The same coherence orders successive gluon emissions in angle, which underlies angular-ordered parton showers and the hump-backed plateau of hadron spectra in jets.
breaks: Gluons carry colour and radiate themselves (C_A vs C_F). Colour-interference terms beyond leading N_c and non-global logarithms have no QED counterpart.

name: Bremsstrahlung, radiation length and EM showers
summary: High-energy electrons lose energy by bremsstrahlung (the QED version of radiation from a decelerated charge) and photons convert to pairs over 9X₀/7. Alternating these processes builds an electromagnetic shower whose depth grows like ln E, which is the basis of electromagnetic calorimetry.

name: Cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (Project 8)
summary: Single β-decay electrons trapped in a magnetic field emit femtowatt cyclotron radiation, and its relativistic frequency gives their energy. Project 8 measured a first tritium spectrum and neutrino-mass limit this way (2023) and aims for ~40 meV sensitivity with atomic tritium.

name: Soft-photon theorem: classical radiation from sudden kicks
summary: The low-frequency Liénard–Wiechert spectrum of charges whose velocities change suddenly is exactly Weinberg's soft factor multiplying any QED amplitude. Its 1/ω photon number is the infrared divergence, which Bloch–Nordsieck summation over unresolved soft photons removes.

name: Classical self-energy and radiation reaction → mass renormalization
summary: A point electron's field energy diverges linearly as its radius goes to zero, and Abraham–Lorentz radiation reaction has runaway solutions. QED softens the divergence to a logarithm (Weisskopf 1939, through positron screening) and absorbs it into the observed mass — the first renormalization.

name: Coherent forward scattering → refractive index (MSW)
summary: A medium's refractive index is fixed by the forward scattering amplitude of its scatterers, the same physics as the optical theorem. Wolfenstein applied this to neutrinos: charged-current forward scattering on electrons gives ν_e an extra potential √2 G_F N_e, which changes the effective mixing in the Sun and Earth.
map: n-1=\frac{2\pi N f(0)}{k^2},\quad V_{CC}=\sqrt2\,G_FN_e,\quad \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}{\rm Im}f(0)

name: Thomson → Klein–Nishina: Compton scattering at tree level
summary: The classical Thomson cross-section 8πr_e²/3 is the ω→0 limit of the tree-level QED Klein–Nishina result. The low-energy theorem guarantees this limit holds to all orders, and Compton scattering was the first QED amplitude checked against experiment.

name: Coherent vs incoherent diffraction as speckle statistics
summary: In diffractive vector-meson production off nuclei, the coherent cross section is the square of the configuration-averaged amplitude and the incoherent part is its variance (Good–Walker). This is the same split as specular versus diffuse speckle scattering in the statistical optics of random media. The coherent t-spectrum images the average gluon density and the incoherent one its event-by-event fluctuations, a key saturation probe at the EIC.
breaks: The average runs over quantum configurations of nucleons and gluon hot spots in the target, not over a classical ensemble of scatterers. Saturation also makes the amplitude non-linear in the density.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: HBT intensity interferometry becomes femtoscopy
summary: Hanbury Brown–Twiss intensity interferometry was invented to measure stellar diameters and became femtoscopy in nuclear physics. Two-pion Bose–Einstein correlations (the GGLP effect, 1960) measure the space-time size of the emitting source, and the HBT radii R_out, R_side and R_long test hydrodynamic expansion and freeze-out. The 'HBT puzzle' (R_out/R_side ≈ 1, against early hydro predictions) was resolved by improved hydrodynamic modelling.
map: C_2(\mathbf q)=1+\lambda|\tilde S(\mathbf q)|^2\approx1+\lambda e^{-R_o^2q_o^2-R_s^2q_s^2-R_l^2q_l^2}\ \leftrightarrow\ g^{(2)}=1+|g^{(1)}|^2
breaks: Stellar HBT measures the spatial coherence of light from a static, distant source. Femtoscopy uses massive identical hadrons from an expanding source, so it measures homogeneity regions tied to the flow, needs Coulomb and strong final-state corrections, and gives anticorrelations for fermions.

name: Nucleon tomography from GPDs
summary: Fourier-transforming generalized parton distributions over transverse momentum transfer gives impact-parameter densities. Exclusive processes at the EIC therefore work as a tomograph that images quarks and gluons in the transverse plane at each momentum fraction x. Interference of DVCS with the calculable Bethe–Heitler amplitude supplies the phase, playing the role of a holographic reference wave.
breaks: What is imaged is a distribution in x and b_⊥ (or a Wigner quasi-distribution), not a real-space picture. GPDs enter observables through convolution integrals that cannot be uniquely inverted, unlike an optical Fourier transform.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

name: Form factors as Fourier transforms of charge density
summary: In the Born approximation, the elastic electron-scattering form factor is the Fourier transform of the charge density, just as the Fraunhofer amplitude is the Fourier transform of an aperture. Hofstadter's diffraction minima mapped nuclear charge distributions, and the slope at Q^2=0 gives the rms radius. The Sachs form factors G_E and G_M extend this to the nucleon.
map: F(\mathbf q)=\int\rho(\mathbf r)e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf r}d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ U(\mathbf k_\perp)\propto\int A(\mathbf x)e^{-i\mathbf k_\perp\cdot\mathbf x}d^2x;\ \ \langle r_E^2\rangle=-6\frac{dG_E}{dQ^2}\Big|_0
breaks: For the nucleon, size and Compton wavelength are comparable, so recoil spoils the 3D Breit-frame Fourier interpretation; only 2D transverse densities in the infinite-momentum frame are rigorous. Two-photon exchange also breaks the one-photon (Born) picture and is the leading explanation of the Rosenbluth versus polarization-transfer discrepancy.

name: Neutron optics: refractive index from scattering length
summary: Slow neutrons travel through matter with a refractive index n = 1 − λ^2 N b_c/2π set by the coherent nuclear scattering length, so they refract and are totally reflected below a critical angle. Neutron guides and supermirrors at research reactors and spallation sources, and ultracold-neutron storage bottles, are built on this geometric optics. The Fermi pseudopotential 2πħ^2 N b_c/m is the zero-energy limit of the nuclear optical potential.
breaks: For most materials n < 1, so the reflection is external rather than internal. The index scales as λ^2 instead of following an electronic resonance, and gravity and absorption visibly bend and weaken the beams.

name: Glauber diffraction theory to Glauber initial states
summary: Glauber's eikonal multiple-scattering theory extended Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction to composite targets through the profile function 1 − e^{iχ}. Its Monte Carlo descendant gives the participant number, binary-collision number and initial eccentricities that seed every hydrodynamic flow calculation. The same Roy Glauber founded the quantum theory of optical coherence.
map: \Gamma(\mathbf b)=1-e^{i\chi(\mathbf b)},\ \ f(\mathbf q)=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int d^2b\,e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf b}\Gamma(\mathbf b);\ \ N_{\rm coll}=\sigma_{NN}^{\rm inel}T_{AB}(b)
breaks: The Monte Carlo Glauber model used for flow keeps only the geometric overlap of nucleons and the inelastic NN cross section. It drops the wave-optical phases of the original theory.

name: Nuclear diffraction scattering and the black disk
summary: High-energy hadron and α scattering on nuclei shows the Fraunhofer pattern of an absorbing disk, with minima at kRθ ≈ 3.83 and 7.02. The total cross section is σ_tot = 2πR^2, half elastic shadow and half absorption, which is the extinction paradox of optics. Coulomb-dominated heavy-ion scattering (large Sommerfeld parameter η) shows Fresnel diffraction and nuclear rainbows instead.

name: Optical pumping for polarized nuclear targets and beams
summary: Circularly polarized laser light transfers angular momentum to atoms. Spin-exchange optical pumping through Rb makes polarized 3He, which serves as an effective polarized neutron target, and strained GaAs photocathodes deliver ~85–90% polarized electron beams at JLab. These beams made the recoil-polarization measurement of G_E/G_M possible, which revealed its disagreement with Rosenbluth separation.

name: Reactor criticality as a Helmholtz eigenproblem
summary: In one-group diffusion theory the critical reactor flux satisfies the Helmholtz equation ∇^2φ + B^2φ = 0. Its fundamental shapes (cos, J_0, sin(πr/R)/r) and geometric buckling eigenvalues are the same as the cavity-mode solutions of electromagnetism. Criticality means the material buckling (k∞ − 1)/L^2 equals the geometric buckling.
breaks: φ is a diffusing density, not a wave, so there is no phase or interference. Boundary conditions apply at an extrapolated surface rather than at conducting walls, and only the fundamental mode survives while higher harmonics decay.

name: RF and crab cavities for the EIC
summary: Electron and ion beams at CEBAF, RHIC and the EIC are accelerated and bunched by the TM010 modes of resonant cavities, many of them superconducting. The EIC adds crab cavities, transverse-deflecting modes that tilt the bunches so they collide head-on despite a 25 mrad crossing angle.

name: Spin vs orbital split of photon and gluon angular momentum
summary: Splitting a gauge field's angular momentum into spin and orbital parts depends on the gauge, and the problem is the same for the photon (optical spin versus orbital angular momentum) and the gluon (ΔG versus L_g in the proton spin budget). The Jaffe–Manohar (canonical) and Ji (kinetic, gauge-invariant) decompositions correspond to canonical versus kinetic momentum under minimal coupling p → p − qA.
map: \mathbf J_\gamma=\epsilon_0\int[\mathbf E\times\mathbf A_\perp+E_i(\mathbf r\times\nabla)A_{\perp i}]d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ \tfrac12=\tfrac12\Delta\Sigma+\Delta G+L_q+L_g
sources: European Muon Collaboration (1988). "A measurement of the spin asymmetry and determination of the structure function g1 in deep inelastic muon-proton scattering". *Phys. Lett. B* 206, 364. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(88)91523-7)

name: Equivalent-photon approximation for photoproduction
summary: The Lorentz-contracted field of a fast charge is equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons proportional to Z^2α (Fermi 1924, Weizsäcker–Williams 1934). This underlies photoproduction at the EIC (Q^2 → 0) and the photonuclear and photon–photon physics of ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC, which serve as EIC precursors.

name: Ultrastrong magnetic fields in heavy-ion collisions
summary: In off-central collisions the Lorentz-contracted Liénard–Wiechert fields of the spectator protons produce eB ~ m_π^2 (~10^14 T), the strongest magnetic fields known. They last a few fm/c, extended by Faraday induction in the conducting QGP. These fields drive searches for the chiral magnetic effect and for charge splittings in directed flow and Λ polarization; the 2022 STAR isobar blind analysis found no predefined CME signature.
map: B\simeq\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{Ze\gamma v}{b^2},\ \ eB\sim m_\pi^2\ (\sim10^{14}\ \mathrm T);\ \ \mathbf J_{\rm CME}=\frac{e^2}{2\pi^2}\mu_5\mathbf B\ (\text{natural units})

name: Spin–orbit coupling: atomic vs nuclear
summary: Atomic spin–orbit coupling comes from the magnetic field in the electron's rest frame, with the Thomas factor ½. Mayer and Jensen's strong nuclear spin–orbit term, which produces the magic numbers, has the same L·S form. In relativistic mean-field theory it comes out of the same Dirac reduction, applied to the large scalar and vector nuclear potentials.
map: H_{so}^{\rm at}=\frac{1}{2m^2c^2}\frac{1}{r}\frac{dV}{dr}\mathbf L\cdot\mathbf S\ \leftrightarrow\ H_{so}^{\rm nuc}\propto\frac{1}{r}\frac{d(V-S)}{dr}\mathbf l\cdot\mathbf s
breaks: The nuclear term is not electromagnetic and is far larger relative to level spacings. Its sign lowers j = l + ½ and creates intruder states, while in atoms spin–orbit is a fine-structure correction of order α^2 with the opposite ordering.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

name: Coulomb barrier and electron screening in fusion
summary: Fusion and α-decay rates are set by tunnelling through the electrostatic barrier Z1Z2e^2/4πε0r, so the Gamow factor exp(-2πη) is pure Coulomb physics. Atomic electrons screen the bare charge and raise low-energy laboratory cross sections by exp(πηU_e/E); this must be removed before S-factors are used for stars, where plasma (Debye) screening takes its place. Measured screening potentials often exceed the adiabatic electrostatic estimate.
map: V_C=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0r},\ \ \eta=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar v},\ \ \frac{\sigma_{\rm scr}}{\sigma_{\rm bare}}\approx e^{\pi\eta U_e/E}
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)

name: Coulomb energy of a charged drop sets the fission limit
summary: The Coulomb term of the semi-empirical mass formula is the electrostatic self-energy of a uniformly charged sphere. Bohr–Wheeler fission theory balances it against surface tension for l=2 shape deformations, which gives the fissility x = E_C/2E_S and the liquid-drop limit Z^2/A ≈ 50. This is the nuclear version of Rayleigh's 1882 instability of a charged conducting droplet.
breaks: A conducting drop carries surface charge while the nucleus carries volume charge, so the critical ratios differ. Real fission barriers, spontaneous fission and the existence of superheavy elements beyond x≈1 come from quantum shell corrections and tunnelling, not from classical electrostatics.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)
